## Landed

Gerrit change 1415 merged to main. Both gates green on patchset 2 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1),
submitted, and the landed commit on origin/main carries the `rebar-ticket:` trailer. Verified
post-merge against origin/main directly: `src/rebar/metrics/analyzer.py` contains zero
occurrences of `ANALYZERS`.

Patchset 1 took a Verified -1 that was NOT a code failure: the branch was cut from an
origin/main that predated `980d`, which added `.github/git-version-floor.txt`, and the CI gate
reads that file as the single source of the Git version floor -- so the gate aborted with
"missing .github/git-version-floor.txt" before any test ran. Rebasing onto current origin/main
resolved it with no code change. Worth remembering: a Verified -1 on a patchset cut from a
stale base can be an infrastructure-file gap rather than anything in the diff -- read the gate
error before assuming the change is at fault.

Closed `plan_defect`: the design itself was wrong. Epic 839b's per-language dispatch was retired
by c23c in favour of direct composition, and it was never viable anyway (the keyword mismatch
between `analyze_or_unavailable` and `scc_loc.analyze`). The dead code survived only because
c23c's removal instruction was conditional prose rather than an acceptance criterion, so no
gate held it -- which is the plan defect, not a coding error.

### One follow-up worth noting, not filed

AC3 as written ("byte-identical `rebar metrics`") is not achievable by ANY change in this repo:
a control of two consecutive runs on an unmodified tree already differs in five ticket-derived
metrics. A future ticket wanting this proof should compare the STRUCTURAL metrics' per-file
breakdown (which files moved) rather than the whole payload byte-for-byte. Recorded here rather
than as a ticket because it is a note about how to phrase a criterion, not a defect in the code
-- happy to file it if the operator wants it tracked.
